title: Local exactness of a sectionwise Cech augmentation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U:I\to\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ any family of opens, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf, $D$ a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves, and $\epsilon:F[0]\to D$ a chain map. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $P(W)(V)=F(W\cap V)$ with restricted $A$-action, and $C^\bullet=\check C^\bullet(U,P)$, the full unnormalized Cech complex. Suppose given natural presheaf isomorphisms $e_p:\operatorname{forget}(D^p)\simeq C^p$ with $\operatorname{forget}(d_D^p)e_{p+1}=e_p d_C^p$ for every $p$. Suppose that on every open $V$, each coordinate of $e_0\epsilon^0$, indexed by $y:\operatorname{Fin}(1)\to I$, is the restriction $F(V)\to F((\prod_lU_{y(l)})\cap V)$. For every $i\in I$, restriction of $\epsilon$ to the open subscheme $U_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. There is no covering assumption, no assertion of global exactness, and no assumption identifying the terms of $D$ with products of open direct images.

proof.text: Fix i and restrict to U_i. Every open V of U_i lies inside U_i. Define the degree-lowering homotopy by projecting to tuples with i inserted first, identifying the additional intersection with U_i with V itself. At degree zero project to the singleton i coordinate. These are natural maps of presheaves of global A-modules and hence of underlying abelian sheaves. The given e_p need not respect the full local O_X-action, so transport the homotopy only after forgetting to abelian sheaves.

In d h+h d the face deleting the inserted first index gives the identity. Every other face cancels the term obtained by deleting the shifted index before insertion, with the opposite sign. The given augmentation formula supplies the degree-zero equation and says that the projection onto i is a left inverse of the augmentation. Transport the identities through e_p; the differential equations identify them with those in D. This yields a homotopy equivalence of the restricted augmentation on underlying abelian sheaves and hence an abelian-sheaf quasi-isomorphism. Forgetting module sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves and reflects exactness (kernels on sections, cokernels by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels), so the module-sheaf augmentation is also a quasi-isomorphism. Empty U_i and the zero module satisfy the same identities; empty I has no i to check. No stalk-product interchange is used.
